name: Synthetic biology and biomanufacturing
summary: Engineered cells and enzymes manufacture useful molecules, materials and biological products.
useCase: A producer designs a microbial strain to make a specialty ingredient, then scales fermentation and purification to a repeatable industrial process.
whyNow: DNA design and synthesis are becoming productive supply chains, while manufacturing economics remain highly product-specific. Twist’s gene shipment growth measures demand for an enabling input, not successful industrial output.

mainstream.scope: Routine engineered-biological production of selected high-value ingredients, enzymes and specialty chemicals.
mainstream.rationale: The most valuable, lower-volume products can absorb development and purification costs. Bulk commodity displacement is a separate, slower case dependent on feedstock, scale and energy economics; some applications will remain uneconomic beyond 2035.

metric.name: Twist synthetic genes shipped
metric.scope: One DNA-synthesis supplier; enabling-input activity proxy
metric.limitations: Fiscal years end September. Genes shipped are research and production inputs, not tonnes of biomanufactured product, unique customers or sector adoption. Product mix and cheaper synthesis can expand units without proportional end-market value.
metric.futureNote: No defensible like-for-like external forecast is available for this KPI. The forward maturity path is a separately labelled analyst scenario, not a numerical adoption forecast.

milestones.text: Twist shipped approximately 372,000 genes in fiscal 2021.
No comparable annual shipment point is included for fiscal 2022.
No comparable annual shipment point is included for fiscal 2023.
Twist reported approximately 772,000 genes shipped in fiscal 2024.
Shipments reached approximately 938,000 genes in fiscal 2025.
Asimov introduced a new engineered genome-integration tool for biotherapeutic production. The latest completed fiscal-year shipment measure retained here is 2025.

tailwinds: Automation makes strain design and screening more repeatable
Specialty products can command prices that support early scale-up
bottlenecks: Biology at laboratory scale may not behave the same in large vessels
Purification and feedstock costs can dominate economics
watchMetrics: Commercial product tonnes and recurring customer orders
Titer, rate and yield together with downstream recovery cost
Plant utilisation, gross margin and cash required per new product
